positions.name: GateRatifiedAsSettledMandate
positions.frame: Is this release-manifest rule being performed as a ratified, already-in-effect mandate — stated and formally specified — rather than proposed, argued for, or still under discussion?
positions.why: Across dimensions these four converge on the same directional read: conviction marks all four 'decision' (a rule performed as settled, not a claim being argued), relational marks all four 'authority-ranking' under the same GateAsMandate reading (a non-negotiable precondition imposed rather than described), and register marks all four with the same formal/technical LabelledGateSpecification signature — src-1 states the gate in prose ('now requires... before it ships'), and src-3/src-4/src-5 restate and extend it as bolded label-value fields (Gate/Scope/Owner) in the same protocol vocabulary. The set holds together as one performed specification: what the gate is, where it applies, who owns it — src-2's incident-count justification is a distinct 'claim'-register, market-pricing rationale for the gate rather than a restatement of it, so it does not share this direction.
